design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (pap_supply_replenishment, Medicare world). frozen_time 2026-10-12 10:20:00 EDT.

0. DRAW AND SCOPE. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 4, 5]}. Assignment: resupply_ext_refill_request_items (root) 5 factors, resupply_ext_covered_filter_units 4, resupply_ext_wrong_cushion_reship_units 5, resupply_ext_continued_use_proof_date 5. Nothing was occupied before this task (it is task 0). It claims four policies and four tools: confirm_refill_request_b3535d21 (owner=user), ship_covered_refill_e8c1261e, send_no_charge_replacement_8a217fc0, record_continued_use_proof_c97fce72. Headroom left for task 1 (draw 3 prerequisites, factors [4, 4, 4, 4]): the self-pay subscription side of the charter — self-pay line pricing (resupply_self_pay_pricing, subscription discount, backfill), shipping charges (resupply_shipping), the supply order renewal (resupply_order_renew's rx_date), schedule changes and preference updates — none of which this task touches. Route-around note: the base resupply charter's holdings and contacts carry no numeric field, so the only numeric writes are shipment lines; the root problem's scored value is therefore the item list a refill request records (a fixed-format string), and the proof problem's scored value is a date; both are computed by ordered bindings exactly like a number.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Loretta Szymanski (Original Medicare Part B primary, Medicare Supplement Plan G secondary, patient-owned Auto-Adjusting CPAP, nasal pillows, humidifier, standard tubing) only asks to order whatever supplies she is due for. The desk must (a) read from the refill-request policy that the item list is fixed only after three record states hold, (b) find in the records that none of them holds — a 2026-09-28 filter confirmation at its last shipping day still unanswered, a 2026-09-04 line that shipped full face cushions to a nasal-pillows patient with no reship, and a continued-use date (2025-11-14) older than the credited date of the governing proof on the device record (download 2026-10-02) — (c) work out from the other policies which write brings each state about and compute each write's value, and (d) only then compute the item list and hand Loretta the request step. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling shipment and contact history and the other product's (PAP device) records, and arithmetic; no tool choice is ambiguous because every tool is reached only through its policy's target_tool.

2. POLICIES CLAIMED. All four are new extended policies. base_policy_refs: request -> [resupply_refill_confirmation] (subject resupply_refill_confirmed); filter units -> [resupply_agg_schedule_match, resupply_refill_confirmation, resupply_evt_shipment, resupply_item_compatibility, resupply_shipping, resupply_self_pay_pricing] (every base policy whose subject includes resupply_item_shipped); reship -> [resupply_replacement_rules]; proof -> [resupply_order_continuity]. Triggers: request on_request; the other three state_due (each is owed by the records whatever she called about: a confirmation at its deadline must ship, a line shipped in error must be reshipped, a newer proof on the device record must be carried onto the enrollment). Overwrite: the request policy declares one overwrite of resupply_refill_confirmation's sentence 'A refill is confirmed only on the patient's own statement of the items wanted and their supply status.' replaced by 'For a refill request the patient places on a phone call, and only for such a request, a refill is confirmed on the patient's own answer in the call, asking for the items that are due and reporting their supply as nearly exhausted, and the items it records are the request's item list; every other refill confirmation remains under the base rule.' (the base gate binds the enrollment id to a caller statement, which no caller can state; the extension keeps the patient's own answer as the authority and fixes the list from the records). The covered-filter policy declares an overwrite of resupply_evt_shipment's covered-period sentence ('the units shipped on one line cover units divided by qty times months ...') with its own: a filter line covers the months shipped, counted from the ship date. The reship and proof policies declare overwrite [] — base has no provision for the reship quantity or the proof date.

3. FACTOR CARD (evidence rows and the figure each factor's baseline gives on this world; recomputed by the harness and by check_compute).
 resupply_ext_continued_use_proof_date (result 2026-10-02; all baselines 2026-10-06):
  use_hours_bar [parameter, cross-difficulty pap]: device status patient_owned, setup 2021-02-15 (67 months) -> 1.5 h (tier 'owns, setup 36+ months'); newest download avg 1.8 passes; baseline class 4 h -> 2026-10-06.
  window_nights_bar [parameter, pap]: class modem_data_required true, download taken 2 days after the window -> 21 nights; 26 passes; baseline 30 -> 2026-10-06.
  four_hour_share_bar [parameter, pap]: re-evaluation documenting benefit 2026-10-06 -> 40 percent; 11/26 = 42.3 passes; baseline 70 -> 2026-10-06.
  credited_night [parameter, pap]: no re-evaluation dated on or within 7 days before the download, taken within 7 days of its window -> download date 2026-10-02; baseline last night 2026-09-30.
  governing_kind [method]: either-kind schedule, proving window ended 12 days ago -> download governs; baseline newest of both -> 2026-10-06.
  Near-miss: the 2026-10-06 re-evaluation is newer than the download; a reader who stops at 'newest proof' records 2026-10-06; the governing rule sets it aside.
 resupply_ext_covered_filter_units (result 2; all baselines 1):
  line_span [parameter, multi-source: enrollment date x filter-line count]: enrolled 67 months, four A7038 coverage lines in 12 months (2025-12-08, 2026-02-09, 2026-05-11, 2026-08-05) -> 3 months; baseline 1 month -> 0.
  monthly_filter_rate [method, cross-difficulty pap: allowance as it stands / allowance scaled to measured use (allowance x newest download hours / 8, rounded up, capped) / fixed one a month]: newest met download 2026-07-03 (5.4 h, within 6 months) -> allowance 2; baseline 1 a month -> 1. Near-miss: the newest download (2026-10-02) is low-use (1.8 h) but did not meet the standard, so it does not decide the rate.
  lapsed_month_anchor [parameter]: filters ran out 2026-09-04 before the 2026-09-28 confirmation -> lapse date 2026-09-04, 1 month dropped; baseline (nothing dropped) -> 4.
  held_supply_months [parameter]: one decline 2026-09-15, 13 days before the confirmation -> 1 month kept back; baseline -> 4.
 resupply_ext_wrong_cushion_reship_units (result 5; all baselines 3 = the replaced line's units):
  reship_monthly_rate [parameter]: A7033's latest line (6 units, 3 months) carried 2 a month = allowance 2 -> 2; baseline replaced rate 1 -> 3.
  period_share [method: whole months only / no months / whole months plus the start month]: handled 38 days after 2026-09-04 -> whole months only from the start date, 1; baseline (whole months plus the start month, 2) -> 7.
  remainder_start [parameter]: pillows ran out 2026-09-07 before today -> start date 2026-10-12; baseline start date 2026-09-04 (2 whole months) -> 7.
  letdown_months [parameter]: one earlier carrier_lost reship (2025-12-22) -> +1 month; baseline -> 3.
  went_without_spares [parameter]: 35 days without pillows -> +1 unit; baseline -> 4.
 resupply_ext_refill_request_items (result A7034,A7037; all baselines A7033):
  nocharge_period_rule [method]: wrong_item/carrier_lost reships on file -> no-charge lines count at their own covered-through (A7033 to 2026-12-03); baseline -> A7033,A7034,A7037.
  cash_period_rule [method]: a self-pay A7046 line (2026-08-20, through 2027-02-19) -> counts; baseline -> A7034,A7037,A7046.
  answering_lead [parameter]: 8 confirmations, 1 decline in 6 months -> 3 days; baseline -> A7037.
  proof_recency_lead [parameter]: continued-use date 2026-10-02 (after the proof write) -> 5 days; baseline -> A7037.
  tenure_lead [parameter]: 67 months enrolled -> 4 days; baseline -> A7037.
 Task floors: multi-source line_span; cross-difficulty factors read the PAP device record and its pap_service rows (seeded: pap_holdings 1, pap_service 5).

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Filter line (step 10): resupply_evt_shipment.enrollment_active (status active, evidence resupply_holdings.status); resupply_evt_shipment.not_too_early (time; anchor resupply_shipments.covers_through_date of the latest A7038 coverage line 2026-09-04; ship_no_earlier_days 10 counting back with the boundary day included -> first allowed day 2026-08-25; 2026-10-12 passes; just before 2026-08-24 fails); resupply_refill_confirmation.confirmation_fresh (anchor contact_date 2026-09-28, refill_contact_lead_days 14 counting from the day after, boundary included -> last day 2026-10-12 = today; 2026-10-13 would fail). The base gate is declared superseded by the standing-order policy of task 1, whose replacing sentence keeps exactly this window for every line that rests on a refill confirmation, exempts the automatic-shipment standing-order line of the Self-Pay Supply Subscription, leaves to the base rule whether a coverage-billed line must rest on a request, and holds no no-charge reship to the window (so the step-12 reship is not barred); the evidence is still recorded in base_preconditions, and the gate no longer appears in temporal_feasibility because the structured gate is retired. Schedule match, compatibility, shipping and self-pay pricing are policy_scope for this subject. Reship (step 12): resupply_replacement_rules.one_replacement_per_reason (dedup on original_line_id + replacement_reason; no no-charge row names the 2026-09-04 line). Proof (step 8): resupply_order_continuity has no structured gate; proof comes from the device record's download, never from the patient. Request (step 14): the base patient_request gate is retired by the declared overwrite; the patient's own answer is in the persona.

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Filter line: object = the 2026-09-28 confirmation (resupply_contact_id passed to the tool), item A7038, billed to the enrollment's coverage (Original Medicare Part B). Reship: object = the 2026-09-04 A7031 line (original_line_id), replaced by the fitting item A7033; the other cushion lines (2026-03-09, 2026-06-08 A7033) fit and are excluded; the 2025-12-22 no-charge row replaced a filter line and is only counted as an earlier let-down. Proof: object = the enrollment's continued-use date; the evidence is the device record's newest download. Request: object = today's refill confirmation on the enrollment. Each seeded covered line carries Medicare's 80 percent payment and the 20 percent coinsurance the payer assigned; the coverage-account postings of that coinsurance (settled by the Plan G crossover) belong to the coverage difficulty and lie outside this task's closure, so they are not seeded; both coverage records show a 0.00 patient balance.

6. WORLD ROWS AND WHY THEY EXIST. resupply_shipments: filter lines (span count, run-out, anchor), pillow lines (fitting item's rate and run-out), the A7031 line (the error), headgear/tubing/interface/chamber lines (item list run-outs at 49, 14, 22 and 14 days), the cash chamber (cash rule), the carrier_lost reship (let-down count and the no-charge rule tier). resupply_contacts: 11 confirmations and 1 decline (answering lead, held supply, the open 2026-09-28 confirmation). pap_service: four downloads and one re-evaluation (proof tests, filter rate). Removing the 2026-09-15 decline changes the filter units to 4; removing the cash chamber adds A7046 to the list; removing the carrier_lost reship changes the reship to 3 (no let-down month); the no-charge rule still takes its first tier because today's wrong_item reship stands before the request is computed. Automatic clauses checked: no hold is owed (supply order 2026-02-09 and proof 2025-11-14 are both within 12 months; device patient_owned; coverage active); no hold expiry; no outstanding coverage balance. No cache field is used.

7. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root resupply_ext_refill_request_items; three parallel edges, all value_input, all state form, stated in the root's rule:
 -> covered filter units: 'The item list is fixed only after every earlier refill confirmation naming disposable filters whose last shipping day falls on the day of the request stands answered by a coverage-billed disposable-filter line shipped on or after its contact date.' False at opening: contact 2026-09-28 (A7038) has no A7038 coverage line on or after it (latest 2026-08-05). Only the covered-line write books a coverage-billed shipped line. Skipping it: item list A7034,A7037,A7038.
 -> wrong-cushion reship: 'No item list is fixed until the newest coverage-billed line that shipped a cushion item not fitting the recorded mask style stands answered by a no-charge reship of the fitting cushion item.' False: line 2026-09-04 A7031 vs mask_style nasal_pillows, no no-charge row names it. Only the no-charge replacement write creates such a row. Skipping it: A7033,A7034,A7037.
 -> proof date: 'The item list is fixed only after the enrollment's continued-use date is no older than the credited date of the proof of continued use that governs on the device record.' False: last_continued_use_date 2025-11-14 vs download 2026-10-02. Only the proof write changes that field. Skipping it: A7037.
 Four-point test: each sentence has an ordering connective (only after / not ... until), names a record state (a coverage-billed line, a no-charge reship, the continued-use date) and no action, tool, id or code token, and its scope matches the edge's condition. Two run in the affirmative direction and one in the negated direction. Resolution order: proof, filter line, reship, request (any order of the first three; see order_uniqueness). The customer's own write is the root (owner=user).

8. PERSONA. Loretta volunteers only her goal (order what she is due for, mailed as usual) and identity on request (phone 7245550417, date of birth 1950-08-14; ZIP and email only if asked). She answers questions about earlier texts and the September box vaguely and only when asked; she agrees to steps the agent explains, does not raise any extra ask, places the request with the items read to her and 'nearly used up', and ends after hearing it is in.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION AND REPLAY. Reads: find_customers (phone), verify_customer_identity (phone + DOB), find_resupply_holdings, find_resupply_contacts, find_resupply_shipments, find_pap_holdings, find_pap_service, find_coverage_holdings. Writes: record_continued_use_proof_c97fce72(2026-10-02); ship_covered_refill_e8c1261e(contact 2026-09-28, A7038, 2, through 2026-11-11, ground); send_no_charge_replacement_8a217fc0(line 2026-09-04, wrong_item, A7033, 5, through 2026-12-03, ground); hand over confirm_refill_request_b3535d21(A7034,A7037, nearly_exhausted). Harness output (evalh.py replay with the real tools, identical to check_compute): proof 2026-10-02 (baseline 2026-10-06); filter 2 (baseline 1); reship 5 (baseline 3); request A7034,A7037 (baseline A7033); per-factor figures as in section 3; all six orders of the three prerequisites give terminal hash e9e94ce77c19.

10. DRAFT FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Reading only the published rules, tool schemas and the finder returns: the request rule's three sentences point at the open confirmation, the A7031 line and the proof date; each depended-on rule names its own write and how to size it; applying them gives 2026-10-02, 2 filters through 2026-11-11, 5 pillow pairs through 2026-12-03, then horizon 22 and list A7034,A7037 — matching gold.

11. REVISIONS. (r1) use_hours_bar fall-through was 'no separate test', which left the factor decorative (1.8 h passed either way); the standard method was rewritten to state the class's three compliance figures and the fall-through became the class's compliance minimum hours; re-run: baseline 2026-10-06, factor bites. (r2) governing_kind declared cross-difficulty but its bindings read no PAP primitive; cross_difficulty set to null. (r3) cash_period_rule had no record primitive in its bindings; cash_any now also counts self-pay lines. (r5) after task 1 declared its overwrite of the confirmation_fresh clause, the temporal_feasibility entry for that gate was removed (the solvability gate treats the retired gate as declared but not required). (r4) replay reported 23 seeded rows outside the gold closure (22 coverage-ledger postings and the Plan G record) and two empty coverage_id values read as dangling keys: the ledger postings were dropped as outside this task, a find_coverage_holdings read was added (it is the evidence that the line bills the active primary record), and the no-charge and self-pay seed rows carry a null coverage_id.

12. ROUND 2 REWORK (policy-task audit revision 0: _difficulty.md, 0.md). Symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run.
 (F-G1 / F-0.1 / F-0.4) The filter edge waited on every confirmation that 'has reached the last day it may ship' and on 'a coverage-billed line for each item it names'; that includes passed confirmations (2026-08-31 'A7033', last day 2026-09-14) that no lawful write can answer, and items the filter policy does not size. The sentence now reads 'The item list is fixed only after every earlier refill confirmation naming disposable filters whose last shipping day falls on the day of the request stands answered by a coverage-billed disposable-filter line shipped on or after its contact date.' and the condition says the same. On this world it names exactly one record, the 2026-09-28 confirmation; the filter line written today answers it, so the condition holds in the gold terminal state.
 (F-G2 / F-0.2) The proof edge waited on 'the newest proof', but the proof policy records the governing proof. The sentence now reads 'The item list is fixed only after the enrollment's continued-use date is no older than the credited date of the proof of continued use that governs on the device record.' The proof rule's opening sentence now says the date is brought up only when the governing proof's credited date is newer, and compute implements that check (result = governing if newer than the recorded date). 2026-10-02 is the only value consistent with both texts.
 (F-G3 / F-0.3) The filter rule counted a line's months 'from an anchor' and shipped sub-allowance monthly rates, which the base units/qty covered-period sentence cannot express. The filter policy now declares an overwrite of that base clause and states 'A disposable-filter line covers the months shipped, counted from the ship date, and its covered-through date is the day before the same day of the month that many months later.' The lapse sentence now speaks of a 'lapse date' for dropped months only. Covered-through 2026-11-11 is now entailed by the policy's own sentence.
 (F-G4 / F-0.5) The filter policy had no honest method. monthly_filter_rate is now a method: allowance as it stands / allowance scaled to measured use (allowance x newest download's average hours / 8, rounded up, capped at the allowance) / fixed one a month. lapsed_month_anchor is relabelled parameter. Values unchanged (2 units; per-factor baselines 0 / 1 / 4 / 4; all-baseline 1).
 (F-G6 / F-0.6) credited_night (proof) and remainder_start (reship) relabelled parameter; the proof policy keeps governing_kind and the reship policy keeps period_share as methods. credited_night's first tier, which credited the same date as its second tier, now reads 'the newest re-evaluation documenting benefit is dated on or no more than 7 days before the day the download was taken' (visit date credited); compute compares the newest re-evaluation's date with the download date instead of testing equality.
 (S2 class, edge naming one record) The reship edge now says 'the newest coverage-billed line that shipped a cushion item not fitting the recorded mask style', matching the reship compute (newest non-fitting line).
 (F-G8 / F-0.8 divergences) The decline tier now requires the decline to be dated on or before the confirmation (compute: last_decline <= confirmed_on) and speaks of declines 'dated less than two whole months before the ship date' (the within_months window). The request rule's tubing cash tier now says 'no self-pay line for an item of the recorded equipment but one for the tubing type not in use'. The filter and request rules now state that a coverage-billed line later taken back by a payer still counts, which is what compute does. The request rule now states that these supply dates serve the item list only.
 (F-G9 docstrings) The refill-request, covered-line and shipping-charge docstrings no longer carry sequence hints.
 Re-run: check_compute --task 0 gives proof 2026-10-02, filters 2, reship 5, list A7034,A7037, with factor and baseline figures unchanged; the terminal hash is unchanged because no tool body changed.

13. ROUND 3 REWORK (render_r1_source_mismatches.md items 1, 3, 6, 8; policy audit rev 2 N1, N2).
 (item 1 / N1) The filter overwrite's replacement now names its own scope: 'For a coverage-billed disposable-filter line booked under this rule, and only for such a line, the line covers the months shipped, counted from the ship date ...; every other line that an item limit dates remains under the base covered-period rule, while a no-charge reship, which counts toward no limit, and a standing-order line on the Self-Pay Supply Subscription, which has no unit limits, take the covered-through dates their own rules state.' Covered-through 2026-11-11 is unchanged.
 (N2) The filter rule now says its run-out date 'serves only the months dropped here', while shipping timing follows the base covered-through measure, from which a reversed line drops out. resupply_evt_line_reversal is now cited in the filter and request policies' base_policy_refs. The request rule already scopes its dates to the item list.
 (item 3) In the reship policy, period_share's tier was defined on remainder_start's output (the remainder). The standard paragraph now defines both terms itself: the months are counted from a start date (the replaced line's ship date) to the replaced line's covered-through date, as whole months plus one for the start month. remainder_start sets the start date (handling day / the earlier supply's run-out day / the ship date). period_share sets how the months are counted (whole months only / none / whole months plus the start month). Each tier now refers only to standard-paragraph terms. Value unchanged at 5. period_share's single-factor baseline is now 7 (start 2026-10-12, 2 months counted), not 9. The all-baseline stays 3.
 (item 8 and overwrite-scope class) The refill-request overwrite's replacement is scoped: 'For a refill request the patient places on a phone call, and only for such a request, ...; every other refill confirmation remains under the base rule.' A new sentence limits call requests to schedules whose accepted channels include phone calls. Medicare Part B accepts phone_call, so the gold request stands.
 (item 6 class) Docstrings no longer claim effects the bodies lack: the covered-line tool no longer says the line is tied to the confirmation (the contact id is now described as identifying the booking only) or that amounts change when a remittance arrives; the style tool no longer says the style decides the standing order.
 Re-run: check_compute --task 0 gives 2026-10-02, 2, 5, A7034,A7037.

14. ROUND 4 REWORK (policy audit rev 3 R9, N4, N5; overwrite-scope class).
 (R9) The standing-order policy's confirmation-freshness replacement is back to the round-2 scope: a line that rests on a refill confirmation still ships within the schedule's lead days; the Self-Pay standing-order line for an automatic-shipment patient ships on its cycle; whether a coverage-billed line must rest on a request still follows base sentence 1 (so a Commercial HMO/PPO auto-ship line needs none); a no-charge reship is named as outside the window. On this world the step-12 reship (A7033 x5, replaces 0a1433fd) rests on no confirmation and is not barred; the step-10 filter line rests on the 2026-09-28 confirmation (last day 2026-10-12 = today).
 (N5) The filter overwrite's 'every other' clause now reaches only lines an item limit dates (the base clause's subject) and names the no-charge reship (counts toward no limit) and the Self-Pay standing-order line (no unit limits) as dated by their own rules. The seeded carrier_lost reship and the A7046 self-pay line keep their dates.
 (class sweep) Every overwrite's replacement was re-read against its superseded clause: the ground catch-up replacement now says 'every other shipment that went out by ground'; the rush replacement now covers every expedited shipment (once per shipment, transit promise included) instead of only today's; the subscription-discount replacement now names shipping charges as outside it; the refill-request replacement already reaches exactly refill confirmations.
 Values unchanged: check_compute --task 0 gives 2026-10-02, 2, 5, A7034,A7037.

15. ROUND 5 REWORK (kb_r1_source_leak.md; policy_kb rev 1 coverage note).
 (source leak) The refill-request tool's items_requested description gave 'for example the form A7034,A7037', which is this task's scored item list. The example is gone; the description now states the format only (HCPCS codes, comma separated, ascending, no spaces, each code in full as one capital letter and four digits, named once). No other docstring or parameter description of the eight tools carries an example value (the enum lists are the full enum sets). Tool names, signatures and bodies are unchanged.
 (modem wording) The nights-bar tiers now say 'a device class whose compliance is proven only from modem or card data', the base pap attribute wording for modem_data_required ('compliance is proven only from device modem or card data'), in place of 'reports by modem'. The tier taken here is unchanged (Auto-Adjusting CPAP, modem_data_required true, pulled 2 days after its last night -> 21 nights).
 Values unchanged: check_compute --task 0 gives 2026-10-02, 2, 5, A7034,A7037.
user_scenario:
You are Loretta Szymanski, a 76-year-old retired school secretary who lives at 418 Mace Street in Greensburg, Pennsylvania. You have slept with a CPAP machine and nasal pillows for about five years and you get your mask supplies from Summit Ridge Home Medical, billed to your Medicare. A reminder text came this week, so you are calling to order whatever supplies you are due for now. You honestly do not keep track of which pieces are due when, so you want the agent to look that up for you; you just want the things you are due for sent to your house the usual way. You are in no rush and you are not travelling anywhere.
You open by giving your name and saying why you are calling. When the agent asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 7245550417. When they need something else to confirm it is you, you give your date of birth, August 14, 1950 (1950-08-14); only if they ask for more do you add your ZIP code, 15601, or your email, lszymanski50@zoominternet.net. Your Medicare card is in your purse but you would rather not read numbers off it unless the agent truly needs them.
If the agent asks how the supplies should come, you say regular mail to the house is fine, the way it always comes. If they ask whether the supplies you are due for are running low, you say yes, they are about used up. If they ask about earlier texts you answered, you say you answer the reminder texts when they come and cannot remember which items each one was about. If they ask about the boxes you received lately, you say a box came in September that you put in the closet without looking closely, because you still had a few pillows left.
Whenever the agent explains that something has to be taken care of on your account first, or that they are sending something out to you at no charge, you say that is fine and thank them; you do not ask for anything extra. When the agent reads you the list of supplies you can ask for today and hands you the step to place the request yourself, you place it exactly with the items they read to you and say your supply is nearly used up. Once the agent tells you the request is in, you thank them warmly and end the call.

request_alignment.claim: The patient wants to order the supplies she is due for, sent by regular mail.
evidence: user_scenario:calling to order whatever supplies you are due for now
user_scenario:regular mail to the house is fine

gold_actions.business_effect: The enrollment's continued-use date moves from 2025-11-14 to 2026-10-02, the date credited to the proof of continued use that governs on the device record.

request_binding.action_semantics: The device record holds a compliance download taken 2026-10-02 that is newer than the enrollment's continued-use date 2025-11-14; the proof policy makes bringing the enrollment up to it a standing obligation, and the refill request she asked for waits on it. Only the continued-use proof tool records that date; no other write changes it.

discriminator.business_meaning: a newer proof of continued use on the device record than on the enrollment

stage_provenance.fact: the enrollment carries the newer proof of continued use

base_preconditions.condition: A newer proof of continued use is recorded only from a compliance download or practitioner note of the kind the schedule's continued_use_basis accepts, never from the patient's own account; the proof here is the device record's 2026-10-02 compliance download.

gold_actions.business_effect: A coverage-billed line of 2 disposable filters (A7038) ships today against the 2026-09-28 confirmation, covering through 2026-11-11.

request_binding.action_semantics: The 2026-09-28 refill confirmation names A7038 and reaches its last shipping day today (14 days, boundary included); no coverage-billed A7038 line has shipped since. A confirmed covered item ships on a coverage-billed shipped line, which only this tool writes; a self-pay line or a no-charge replacement would bill the wrong party.

discriminator.business_meaning: a covered item named on a refill confirmation at its last shipping day

stage_provenance.fact: the filters ship today against the confirmation

base_preconditions.condition: The line is billed under the schedule of the active primary coverage record: the enrollment follows the Medicare Part B Resupply Schedule and bills Original Medicare Part B, which is active and primary.
